subject.title: [Bug]: browser in docker hidden in cache folder

question: Should OpenClaw keep `/home/node/.cache/ms-playwright` as the Docker browser cache contract now that runtime autodetection exists, or move browser assets to `/opt` and expose stable `chrome`/`chromium` commands on PATH?
rationale: Current source, tests, docs, and the latest release still encode the home-cache contract, while prior `/opt` attempts exposed upgrade and proof gaps that automation should not resolve as a product choice.

options.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
options.body: Treat the merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and leave `/opt` plus PATH aliases out unless stronger migration evidence appears.

options.title: Approve `/opt` Plus PATH Migration
options.body: Require a focused Dockerfile/docs/test change with live proof for browser-enabled, browser-disabled, runtime-install, and existing-cache upgrade scenarios.

options.title: Narrow To PATH Aliases
options.body: Keep the current cache location but add layout-aware `chrome` and `chromium` aliases only if maintainers want that Docker command surface.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
recommendation.body: Treat the merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and leave `/opt` plus PATH aliases out unless stronger migration evidence appears.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the clearest maintainer-facing close rationale for the prior same-repository `/opt/playwright` attempt and tied it to required container proof.
